name: PM SVANidhi (PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi)
ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
target_audience: Urban and peri-urban street vendors, hawkers, thelawalas, food stall operators, artisans
subsidy_info: 7% interest subsidy per annum on timely repayment, plus up to ₹1,200/year cashback on digital transactions
short_description: Micro-credit scheme providing collateral-free working capital loans up to ₹50,000 with 7% interest subsidy and digital transaction cashback for urban street vendors.
eligibility: Must be an urban or peri-urban street vendor engaged in vending on or before March 24, 2020 (or identified in subsequent urban surveys).
Possession of Certificate of Vending (CoV) / Identity Card issued by Urban Local Bodies (ULB) or Town Vending Committee (TVC).
Vendors left out of ULB surveys can obtain a Letter of Recommendation (LoR) from the ULB / Town Vending Committee.
Vendors from surrounding peri-urban/rural areas vending within geographic limits of ULBs are eligible with a LoR.
benefits: Initial working capital loan of up to ₹10,000 with tenure of 1 year without any collateral.
Enhanced credit limit of ₹20,000 in 2nd tranche and ₹50,000 in 3rd tranche upon timely or early repayment.
7% interest subsidy credited directly to vendor's bank account quarterly on timely repayment.
No pre-payment penalty on early closure of loans.
Cashback incentives of ₹100 per month (up to ₹1,200 per year) for adopting digital transactions (UPI/QR code).
documents_required: Aadhaar Card linked with mobile number
Voter ID / Driving License (as additional identity proof)
Certificate of Vending (CoV) or Identity Card or Letter of Recommendation (LoR) from ULB
Active Bank Account details (Bank Passbook / Cancelled Cheque)
application_steps: Step 1: Check your name in the street vendor survey list on the PM SVANidhi portal (pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in) or visit your local Urban Local Body (Nagar Nigam/Municipality).
Step 2: If not listed in survey, apply for a Letter of Recommendation (LoR) at your local ULB or Common Service Centre (CSC).
Step 3: Register and apply online at pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in or through a nearby CSC / banking correspondent (Bank Sakhi / BC).
Step 4: Upload Aadhaar, CoV/LoR, and bank account details.
Step 5: Select your preferred lending institution (Public Sector Banks, Regional Rural Banks, Small Finance Banks, NBFCs/MFIs).
Step 6: Loan is sanctioned and disbursed directly into your bank account after verification.

name: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY)
ministry: Ministry of Finance / Department of Financial Services
target_audience: Non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises, food carts, retail shops, repair stalls, small manufacturers
max_benefit: Up to ₹20 Lakhs across 3 categories: Shishu (up to ₹50k), Kishore (₹50k–₹5L), Tarun (₹5L–₹20L)
subsidy_info: No upfront subsidy, but loans are completely collateral-free with low processing fees (zero fee for Shishu loans)
short_description: Collateral-free institutional credit up to ₹20 Lakhs for micro-enterprises across Shishu (up to ₹50k), Kishore (₹50k-₹5L), and Tarun (₹5L-₹20L) categories.
eligibility: Any Indian citizen who has a business plan for a non-farm sector income-generating activity.
Manufacturing, processing, trading, food service stalls, or service sector enterprises.
Must not be a defaulter to any bank or financial institution.
Should have satisfactory credit track record if existing borrower.
benefits: Shishu Category: Loans up to ₹50,000 for new businesses, street vendors, and starting micro units with zero processing fees.
Kishore Category: Loans from ₹50,000 up to ₹5,00,000 for expanding inventory, equipment, or working capital.
Tarun Category: Loans from ₹5,00,000 up to ₹20,00,000 for established small enterprises scaling up operations.
MUDRA Card: A RuPay debit card providing working capital credit facility that can be drawn as needed at ATMs/POS.
No collateral or third-party guarantee required under the Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU).
documents_required: Proof of Identity: Aadhaar Card / Voter ID / PAN Card / Passport
Proof of Residence: Utility bill / Ration card / Aadhaar
Quotation of machinery / items / inventory to be purchased
Proof of business address and business establishment (trade license / registration if available)
Bank statement for last 6 months (for Kishore & Tarun categories)
application_steps: Step 1: Choose the category suited to your requirement (Shishu for up to ₹50,000; Kishore for up to ₹5,00,000).
Step 2: Prepare your business proposal with basic cost estimates for equipment/inventory.
Step 3: Apply online on the Udyamimitra portal (udyamimitra.in) or visit any Commercial Bank, RRB, Small Finance Bank, or MFI.
Step 4: Submit the standard MUDRA application form along with KYC documents and quotations.
Step 5: Bank sanctions loan and issues a MUDRA RuPay Card for flexible withdrawals.

name: PM Vishwakarma Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)
target_audience: Traditional artisans, craftspeople, blacksmiths, carpenters, cobblers, tailors, potter/clay workers, basket weavers
max_benefit: ₹15,000 toolkit grant + ₹3,00,000 collateral-free enterprise loan (5% interest)
subsidy_info: Concessional interest rate of 5% with government providing interest subvention up to 8%; ₹15,000 e-voucher for modern tools
short_description: Comprehensive support for traditional artisans including ₹15,000 modern toolkit grant, ₹500/day training stipend, and collateral-free enterprise loans up to ₹3,00,000 at 5% interest.
eligibility: An artisan or craftsperson working with hands and tools in one of the 18 eligible traditional trades (e.g. Carpenter, Blacksmith, Cobbler, Potter, Tailor, Basket/Mat Maker, Barber, Washerman).
Minimum age of 18 years on date of registration.
Should be engaged in the trade concerned on the date of application.
Should not have availed similar credit-based schemes for self-employment (PMEGP, PM MUDRA) in the last 5 years.
Registration is restricted to one member per family.
benefits: Recognition: PM Vishwakarma Certificate and ID Card.
Skill Upgradation: 5-7 days basic training (40 hours) and optional 15+ days advanced training with stipend of ₹500 per day.
Toolkit Incentive: Financial grant of ₹15,000 in form of e-vouchers/digital incentive for purchasing modern toolkits.
Enterprise Development Loan: Collateral-free loan of up to ₹1,00,000 (1st tranche, 18 months) and ₹2,00,000 (2nd tranche, 30 months) at fixed 5% concessional interest rate.
Digital Transaction Incentive: ₹1 per digital transaction for up to 100 transactions per month.
Marketing Support: Onboarding onto open e-commerce networks (ONDC), quality certification, and branding assistance.
documents_required: Trade-specific declaration / proof of engagement in traditional trade
application_steps: Step 1: Visit the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) with Aadhaar and bank details.
Step 2: Biometric authentication and registration on the PM Vishwakarma Portal.
Step 3: Three-stage verification: Gram Panchayat / Urban Local Body verification, followed by District Implementation Committee, and National Committee screening.
Step 4: Receive PM Vishwakarma Digital Certificate & ID Card.
Step 5: Attend basic training and receive ₹15,000 toolkit e-voucher.
Step 6: Apply for 1st tranche loan of ₹1,00,000 through the portal.

name: e-Shram Portal (National Database of Unorganised Workers)
target_audience: All unorganised sector workers, street vendors, domestic helpers, agriculture workers, gig workers
max_benefit: Universal Account Number (UAN) Card + ₹2 Lakh accidental insurance cover + access to social welfare schemes
subsidy_info: Free registration; automatic link to government disaster relief funds and social security pensions
short_description: National registration portal giving informal workers and street vendors a 12-digit UAN card, ₹2 Lakh accidental death/permanent disability cover, and direct access to welfare schemes.
eligibility: Any unorganised worker between 16 and 59 years of age.
Should not be an income tax payee.
Should not be a member of EPFO (Employees' Provident Fund) or ESIC (Employees' State Insurance).
benefits: Universal Account Number (UAN) card valid throughout India.
Accidental Insurance Cover under PMSBY: ₹2,00,000 on death or permanent disability and ₹1,00,000 on partial disability.
Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) during national emergencies or economic crises (e.g. pandemic assistance).
Single-window gateway to social security schemes like PM-SYM pension and Ayushman Bharat.
documents_required: Bank Account Number with IFSC Code
application_steps: Step 1: Self-register on eshram.gov.in or visit a nearby CSC / Seva Kendra.
Step 2: Enter Aadhaar number and verify using OTP sent to registered mobile.
Step 3: Fill in address, educational qualification, occupation (Street Vendor / Hawkers), and bank account details.
Step 4: Download and print your 12-digit e-Shram UAN Card immediately.

name: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
target_audience: Micro and small business owners seeking bank loans without collateral
max_benefit: Credit guarantee cover up to ₹500 Lakhs (₹5 Crores) for collateral-free bank loans
subsidy_info: Up to 85% credit guarantee coverage for micro-enterprises and women/SC/ST entrepreneurs
short_description: Enables banks to provide collateral-free credit facilities to micro and small business owners by offering credit guarantee coverage up to 85%.
eligibility: New and existing Micro and Small Enterprises engaged in manufacturing or service activities, retail trade, or food processing.
Educational institutions, training institutions, and retail traders are also eligible.
Borrower must have a viable business model and Udyam Registration.
benefits: Zero third-party guarantee or tangible collateral needed to obtain bank finance.
Guarantee coverage of up to 85% for loans up to ₹5 Lakhs to micro enterprises.
Guarantee coverage of up to 85% for women-owned enterprises and units in North-East Region.
Substantially lower interest rates due to reduced lending risk for commercial banks.
documents_required: Project Report / Business Plan showing working capital requirement
application_steps: Step 1: Register business on Udyam Registration Portal to get Udyam MSME number.
Step 2: Prepare a brief business profile and project cost estimate.
Step 3: Approach any member lending institution (MLI) including SBI, PNB, Bank of Baroda, or private scheduled banks.
Step 4: Request loan under the CGTMSE guarantee scheme without offering collateral.
Step 5: Bank evaluates project and applies directly to CGTMSE trust for guarantee cover.

name: DAY-NULM (Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Urban Livelihoods Mission)
ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
target_audience: Urban poor, street vendors, Self-Help Groups (SHGs), urban micro-enterprises
max_benefit: Subsidized bank loans up to ₹2 Lakhs for individuals, ₹10 Lakhs for groups; interest above 7% is fully subsidized
subsidy_info: Interest subsidy on all bank loans over 7% per annum; skill training with 100% financial support
short_description: Urban livelihoods mission providing interest subvention over 7% on micro-enterprise loans, dedicated vending zones, and formation of vendor Self-Help Groups.
eligibility: Urban poor and street vendors residing in urban areas.
Individual micro-entrepreneurs or Self Help Groups (SHGs) formed under DAY-NULM.
Minimum 18 years of age.
benefits: Self-Employment Programme (SEP): Financial assistance through bank loans up to ₹2,00,000 for individual micro-enterprises.
Group Enterprises (SEP-G): Financial assistance up to ₹10,00,000 for SHG group enterprises.
Interest Subvention: Difference between the bank interest rate and 7% per annum is refunded as direct interest subsidy.
Support to Urban Street Vendors (SUSV): Creation of dedicated vending zones, ID cards, and social security linkage.
documents_required: Address proof in urban area / Ration card
Vending ID or SHG membership certification
application_steps: Step 1: Contact City Mission Management Unit (CMMU) at your local Municipal Corporation / ULB office.
Step 2: Fill out the Self-Employment Programme (SEP) application form.
Step 3: Task Force committee at ULB reviews and sponsors the application to local banks.
Step 4: Bank sanctions loan with automated interest subvention credited directly to the loan account.

name: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) & Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)
target_audience: All bank account holders, street vendors, unorganised sector workers aged 18 to 70
max_benefit: ₹2 Lakh life cover (PMJJBY) + ₹2 Lakh accidental insurance cover (PMSBY) for less than ₹1.50 per day
subsidy_info: Ultra-low premium: PMSBY is ₹20/year; PMJJBY is ₹436/year, auto-debited annually
short_description: Government-backed life and accident micro-insurance offering ₹2 Lakh life cover and ₹2 Lakh accident cover at a combined annual cost of under ₹460.
eligibility: PMSBY: Any individual aged 18 to 70 years with a savings bank account.
PMJJBY: Any individual aged 18 to 50 years with a savings bank account.
Consent for auto-debit of premium from savings account.
benefits: PMSBY: ₹2,00,000 for accidental death or total permanent disability; ₹1,00,000 for partial permanent disability (Premium: ₹20/year).
PMJJBY: ₹2,00,000 life insurance cover for death due to any cause (Premium: ₹436/year).
Simple one-step enrollment through any bank branch or internet banking.
Instant financial protection for the vendor's family in case of unforeseen emergencies.
documents_required: Aadhaar Card (for KYC and DBT linkage)
application_steps: Step 1: Visit the bank branch where you have a savings account or access your mobile banking app.
Step 2: Submit the 1-page PMSBY and PMJJBY enrollment form with nominee details.
Step 3: Enable annual auto-debit consent.
Step 4: Receive policy certificate via SMS / email.

name: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM)
target_audience: Street vendors, head loaders, rickshaw pullers, domestic workers with monthly income <= ₹15,000
max_benefit: Assured monthly pension of ₹3,000 after attaining age 60
subsidy_info: 50% matching contribution paid by Central Government into vendor's pension fund
short_description: Voluntary contributory pension scheme ensuring ₹3,000 monthly pension post-60 with 50% matching contribution from Central Government for unorganised vendors earning <= ₹15,000/month.
eligibility: Street vendors, hawkers, small shop assistants and unorganised workers.
Entry age between 18 and 40 years.
Monthly income should be ₹15,000 or below.
Should not be covered under EPFO, ESIC, or NPS, and not an income tax payer.
benefits: Guaranteed minimum pension of ₹3,000 per month upon reaching 60 years of age.
Matching 50:50 contribution: If vendor contributes ₹55 to ₹200/month (based on entry age), Central Government matches the exact same amount.
Family pension: In case of demise of pensioner, spouse receives 50% of pension (₹1,500/month).
Easy exit with interest if discontinued before age 60.
documents_required: Savings Bank Account / Jan Dhan Account Passbook
application_steps: Step 1: Visit the nearest Common Services Centre (CSC).
Step 2: Provide Aadhaar and bank account details for biometric verification.
Step 3: Initial contribution amount paid in cash at CSC; system generates Shram Yogi Pension Card.
Step 4: Subsequent monthly contributions auto-debited from linked bank account.
